proposed.text: According to Trap #12 in the Top 50 Traps article, what is the maximum riser height for accessible stairs under BP 344, and how does this differ from the PD 1096 general stair maximum?

options.text: BP 344 accessible stairs: 175 mm maximum riser; PD 1096 general stairs: 200 mm maximum
BP 344 accessible stairs: 150 mm maximum riser; PD 1096 general stairs: 200 mm maximum
BP 344 accessible stairs: 150 mm maximum riser; PD 1096 general stairs: 180 mm maximum
BP 344 accessible stairs: 200 mm maximum riser; PD 1096 general stairs: 250 mm maximum

rationale.summary: Trap #12: BP 344 accessible stairs cap riser at 150 mm; PD 1096 general stairs allow up to 200 mm.
rationale.explanation: Trap #12 in the article. PD 1096 allows risers up to 200 mm for general occupancy stairs. BP 344 is more restrictive for accessible stairs, capping risers at 150 mm. The lower riser height reduces the step height demand on persons with mobility impairments, reducing the energy and muscle force required per step. On the ALE, whenever the question specifies 'accessible staircase,' the BP 344 maximum of 150 mm is the correct answer — not the PD 1096 value of 200 mm.
common_misconceptions: Applying PD 1096's 200 mm maximum to accessible stairs — BP 344 is more restrictive at 150 mm
Selecting 175 mm as a middle ground — there is no middle value; the two standards are 150 mm (BP 344) and 200 mm (PD 1096)

proposed.explanation: Accessible stair riser: 150 mm max (BP 344); general stair riser: 200 mm max (PD 1096) — BP 344 is always more restrictive.
